issue: Simplification: `_restoring_committer_name` (19 lines) monkey-patches `run` and `run_once` on each Loop instance in `make_loop`. An autouse fixture doing `monkeypatch.delenv("GIT_COMMITTER_NAME", raising=False)` is about 3 lines and also covers tests that don't go through `make_loop`. This is the fix R7 originally suggested. The current wrapper works, so the change is optional
reason: The reviewer calls it optional and the wrapper works. Rewriting a working test harness for 16 fewer lines is churn against a green gate; a future test outside make_loop is the trigger to switch to the fixture.

issue: `catchup-probe --state` is optional and resolves the state path by walking up from cwd. The spec says `catchup-probe --state <path>`. This is a documented fix, so it is a small, benign extension.
reason: The optional flag IS the fix cycle 1 asked for (prior R5: the documented bare `autopilot catchup-probe` call failed because --state was required). The reviewer confirms it is benign; the spec text is the thing that was wrong.

issue: `commits_all_loop` interpolates `base` into `git log` as `f"{base}..HEAD"` with no `--end-of-options` or `^{commit}` guard. A `catchup_head_sha` starting with `-` would be read as a git option. The value comes from the agent-written state.json, so this is low risk. A bad sha makes git fail and the result is `full`, so it fails safe.
reason: Not a trust boundary: the value is written by statectl into the loop's own state file, never by external input, and the failure mode the reviewer names is fail-safe (git errors -> full catchup). Validation for a case that cannot arise.

issue: The committer name is a plain string match. Anyone who sets `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=autopilot-loop/<id>` can forge a loop commit. The spec accepts this under Risks, and a forged commit only changes the result from full to delta.
reason: Accepted in the PRD Risks section; the reviewer confirms the worst case is one skipped full catchup in the operator's own repo. Signing loop commits is a larger design decision, not this PRD's.

issue: The first session of a batch gets `autopilot-loop/no-batch`, so the next entry reads one extra full catchup. The spec accepts this under Risks and no code special-cases it.
reason: Accepted in the PRD Risks section (added in cycle 1 as prior R15). Bounded at one extra catchup per batch and fails safe.
